task: Repair the Quality Control Plane Operational Intelligence validator so critical semantic execution routes require an explicit authority category that exactly matches expectedAuthorities, allowing an empty authority array only when the canonical expectedAuthorities scope is empty while preserving fail-closed non-empty authority for architecture-bearing work.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: Sentinel plan-isolation CI #9063 proved a second neutral-scope contradiction in current main: Plan Before Code now truthfully accepts expectedAuthorities=[] for a neutral test-only projection, but validateOperationalIntelligence still requires semanticExecutionRoute.authority to be non-empty for every critical plan. Supplying a fake authority would corrupt the Authority Graph and let semantic route metadata diverge from the plan's canonical expected authority scope.
observableOutcomes: Critical plans must always declare semanticExecutionRoute.authority as an explicit array.
When expectedAuthorities is empty, semanticExecutionRoute.authority=[] is accepted as a truthful neutral route category.
When expectedAuthorities is non-empty, semanticExecutionRoute.authority must also be non-empty.
Semantic route authority must exactly match expectedAuthorities; invented or missing authorities fail closed with a precise machine code.
The blocked Sentinel plan-isolation plan can proceed without fabricating release-infrastructure as an authority.
unresolvedRisks: Conditioning only on array presence without exact equality could allow false authority metadata to pass.
Allowing empty authority too broadly could weaken architecture-bearing critical plans.
Changing the validator without regression coverage could create a silent mismatch between Plan Before Code scope and Operational Intelligence semantics.
The new authority-drift diagnostic must remain deterministic for release-unit child plans as well as ordinary critical plans.

in: Refine only the critical semantic execution route authority validation in scripts/lib/shoperation-operational-intelligence.mjs.
Require explicit authority category presence for every critical route.
Require exact equality between semanticExecutionRoute.authority and plan.expectedAuthorities.
Permit an empty route authority array only when expectedAuthorities is canonically empty.
Add focused regression tests for neutral, missing, false and matching authority cases.
out: No change to Plan Before Code domain/authority projection rules.
No change to Sentinel evaluator semantics.
No change to release-unit materialization, Truth Gate evidence semantics, product runtime or deployment.
No relaxation of MUST_EDIT/MUST_CREATE, PROOF or UNKNOWN route requirements.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This validator protects the semantic route authority declaration used by critical Control Plane work. A permissive mistake could allow false authority metadata, while the current unconditional non-empty rule blocks truthful neutral plans. The fix therefore needs exact equality, negative cases and preservation of all other critical route requirements.

acceptanceCriteria: Critical semanticExecutionRoute.authority must be present as an array even when empty.
Neutral critical plan with expectedAuthorities=[] and route.authority=[] passes the authority-category requirement.
Architecture-bearing critical plan with non-empty expectedAuthorities and route.authority=[] fails closed.
Any route.authority value that differs from expectedAuthorities fails with a dedicated authority-drift diagnostic.
Matching non-empty route authority continues to pass.
MUST_EDIT or child MUST_CREATE, PROOF and UNKNOWN requirements remain unchanged.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth and Lifecycle Closure pass before merge.
invariants: Semantic execution authority may never invent an owner absent from expectedAuthorities.
Semantic execution authority may never omit a canonical expected authority.
Empty authority is truthful only when expectedAuthorities is empty.
Critical route target, proof and unknown-category requirements remain fail closed.
Release-unit child route semantics remain governed by the same authority equality rule.

failureModes: Validator still treats empty neutral authority as missing.
Validator accepts false non-empty authority for a neutral plan.
Validator accepts empty route authority while expectedAuthorities is non-empty.
Authority equality normalization is order-sensitive and creates false drift.
Child transaction route validation diverges from ordinary critical plan validation.
edgeCases: route.authority contains the same authorities in a different order
child route uses mustCreate rather than mustEdit
route.unknown remains non-empty while authority is otherwise valid

alternatives.summary: Require an explicit authority array and exact normalized equality with expectedAuthorities, allowing empty only when the expected scope is empty.
alternatives.reason: Preserves truthful neutral semantics and strengthens fail-closed authority coherence.

alternatives.summary: Keep the validator unchanged and declare a convenient non-empty authority for neutral plans.
alternatives.reason: Would deliberately corrupt authority metadata and undermine the Authority Graph.

alternatives.summary: Treat any authority array, including false non-empty values, as satisfying the critical route requirement.
alternatives.reason: Would remove the contradiction but permit semantic route authority drift.

alternatives.summary: Remove semanticExecutionRoute.authority from critical route requirements.
alternatives.reason: Would weaken critical execution planning and discard useful machine-checkable authority semantics.

specialistReviews.finding: Allowing empty route authority can become a general bypass unless it is tied exactly to the canonical expectedAuthorities scope.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require array presence and exact normalized equality to plan.expectedAuthorities; architecture-bearing scope therefore remains non-empty.

specialistReviews.finding: The current contradiction is caused by two validators representing empty ownership differently.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use expectedAuthorities as the canonical authority envelope and validate semantic route data against it exactly.

specialistReviews.finding: The failure is deterministic and appears only after the preceding neutral ownership prerequisite was correctly fixed.
specialistReviews.resolution: Capture the case with focused positive and negative regression tests before replaying the Sentinel plan.

specialistReviews.finding: The fix must remain a standalone Control Plane prerequisite and not be mixed with the downstream Sentinel test implementation.
specialistReviews.resolution: Prove and merge this validator change first, then reproject the Sentinel branch on fresh main.

challenge.scenario: Neutral critical plan has expectedAuthorities=[] and explicit route.authority=[].
challenge.finding: Current validator incorrectly treats truthful empty authority as absent.
challenge.resolution: Array presence satisfies category explicitness when expected authority scope is empty.

challenge.finding: Merely allowing arrays would accept fabricated authority.
challenge.resolution: Exact normalized equality with expectedAuthorities blocks the false owner.

challenge.scenario: Quality critical plan expects quality-knowledge-system but route.authority=[].
challenge.finding: Empty authority would under-declare architecture-bearing ownership.
challenge.resolution: Non-empty expected authority requires matching non-empty route authority.

challenge.scenario: Quality critical plan declares matching quality-knowledge-system authority.
challenge.finding: Existing legitimate critical planning must remain valid.
challenge.resolution: Exact equality accepts the matching route.

challenge.finding: A missing category is not equivalent to an explicitly neutral category.
challenge.resolution: Require Array.isArray(route.authority) for every critical route.

challenge.finding: Order-only differences must not cause semantic drift.

challenge.resolution: Retain existing child routeTargets rule and apply the same authority equality check.

challenge.finding: Authority coherence must not bypass unresolved semantic relationships.
challenge.resolution: Retain the existing UNKNOWN non-empty blocking rule unchanged.

proofPlan: Commit this plan only against current main and require Plan Before Code PASS.
Add deterministic self/regression cases for neutral empty, missing authority, false authority, empty architecture authority and matching authority.
Require full exact-head Knowledge/Plan/Edit-Time/Incremental/Release Risk/Quality/TypeScript/Build/Completion Truth/Lifecycle proof.
Merge after exact PR-head success, then reproject and continue the Sentinel plan-isolation repair.

requirements.requirement: Critical semantic execution routes must declare an explicit authority category that exactly matches the plan expectedAuthorities scope, including truthful empty authority for neutral scope.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A critical plan with non-empty expectedAuthorities may not pass with an empty semantic route authority.
A neutral plan may not pass with a fabricated semantic route authority absent from expectedAuthorities.

notes: Bounded prerequisite discovered by Sentinel plan-isolation CI #9063 after PR #1045 correctly enabled truthful empty expectedAuthorities for neutral critical plans. This transaction changes only Operational Intelligence semantic route authority validation and its regression proof; the downstream Sentinel implementation remains frozen until this prerequisite merges. Reprojected from the stale prerequisite plan branch onto fresh main 334a2736013461447d4f3269e7ed54e219e60bec after Sentinel probe plan-isolation PR #1049 merged; scope and proof obligations are unchanged. CI #9072 exposed SENTINEL_INTEGRITY_PROOF_DIMENSION_DRIFT for the authority claim because the Completion Contract referenced only test/type/build guards. The canonical GUARD-PLAN-BEFORE-CODE already proves CAP-QUALITY at scope strength 2 with an explicit authority dimension, so it is added as implementation evidence without weakening the claim.
